extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants and peer reviewers (investigators applying for or reviewing R01/R03/R15/R21/R34 Research Project Grants)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions and guidance for reviewers evaluating NIH Research Project Grant (RPG) applications (R01, R03, R15, R21, R34), including criteria used to assign overall impact/priority scores and specific considerations (human subjects, animals, biohazards, resource sharing, budget, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact (R01, R03, R21, R34)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide an overall impact/priority score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The overall impact score is given in consideration of the following review criteria and additional review criteria (as applicable for the project proposed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact (R15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide an overall impact/priority score reflecting likelihood for the project to make an important scientific contribution, provide research opportunities to students, and strengthen the research environment of the institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The score should be given in consideration of the standard review criteria and additional review criteria as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: R03 (Small Research Grant) program-specific guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: R03 supports discrete, well-defined projects that can realistically be completed in two years and that require limited funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because R03 projects are usually limited, applications may not contain extensive detail. Reviewers should evaluate the conceptual framework and general approach. Appropriate justification can be provided via literature citations, data from other sources, or investigator-generated data. Preliminary data are not required (particularly for pilot or feasibility studies).

rubrics_metrics.name: R15 (AREA) program objectives and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectives: (1) provide support for meritorious research, (2) strengthen the research environment of schools not major NIH recipients, and (3) expose undergraduate and graduate students to meritorious research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary data are not required for R15 applications but may be included if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: R21 (Exploratory/Developmental) program-specific guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: R21 supports investigation of novel scientific ideas or new model systems, tools, or technologies with potential for significant impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R21 applications need not have extensive background or preliminary information. Reviewers should focus evaluation on the conceptual framework, level of innovation, and potential to significantly advance knowledge. Justification can be literature citations, other data, or investigator data when available. Preliminary data are not required but may be included if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: R34 (Clinical Trial Planning Grant) program-specific guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: R34 supports development of Phase III clinical trials: establishing the research team, data management/oversight tools, recruitment strategies, finalizing protocol, and preparing operations/procedures manual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R34 is not designed for collection of preliminary data or pilot studies to support rationale; reviewers will focus on the rationale for the proposed clinical trial and the design/protocol of the proposed trial in its current, early form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (R01, R03, R21, R34)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or critical barrier to progress? If aims are achieved, how will scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice be improved?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how successful completion will change concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, services, or preventive interventions that drive the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (R15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or barrier to progress? If aims are achieved, how will scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice be improved?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also consider whether, if funded, the AREA award will have a substantial effect on the school/academic component by strengthening the research environment and exposing students to research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s) (R01, R03, R21, R34)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PD/PIs, collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project? If Early Stage Investigators or New Investigators, do they have appropriate experience and training?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For established investigators, have they demonstrated an ongoing record of accomplishments that have advanced their fields? For collaborative or multi-PD/PI projects, do the investigators have complementary and integrated expertise; are leadership approach, governance, and organizational structure appropriate for the project?

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s) (R15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PD/PIs, collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project? If Early Stage Investigators or New Investigators, do they have appropriate experience and training?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For established investigators, have they demonstrated ongoing accomplishments? For collaborative/multi-PD(s)/PI(s), assess complementary/integrated expertise and leadership/governance structure. Additionally, do the PD(s)/PI(s) have suitable experience in supervising students in research?

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms by utilizing novel theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether concepts/approaches/methodologies/instrumentation/interventions are novel to one field or novel in a broad sense, or whether a refinement, improvement, or new application is proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (R01, R03, R21, R34)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the specific aims?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for presentation of potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success. If early-stage, will the strategy establish feasibility and manage risky aspects? If human subjects/clinical research are involved, reviewers assess: (1) protection of human subjects from research risks, and (2) inclusion/exclusion plans for sex/gender, race, ethnicity, and children, and whether these are justified in terms of scientific goals and research strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (R15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the specific aims?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider potential problems, alternative strategies, benchmarks for success, and whether early-stage work will establish feasibility and manage risky aspects. For clinical research, evaluate plans for human subjects protection and inclusion of minorities and sexes/genders and children. Also assess whether the application provides sufficient evidence the project can stimulate student interest toward biomedical/behavioral science careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment (R01, R03, R21, R34)
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific environment in which the work will be done contribute to the probability of success?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate institutional support, equipment, and other physical resources available, and whether the project benefits from unique features of the environment, subject populations, or collaborative arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment (R15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are institutional support, equipment, and other physical resources adequate for the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess likely availability of well-qualified students to participate and whether the application shows evidence that students have in the past or are likely to pursue careers in biomedical or behavioral sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-exempt human subjects research, the committee will evaluate justification for involvement of human subjects and proposed protections from research risk according to five review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five criteria: (1) risk to subjects, (2) adequacy of protection against risks, (3) potential benefits to subjects and others, (4) importance of the knowledge to be gained, and (5) data and safety monitoring for clinical trials. For research meeting exemption criteria, evaluate: (1) justification for exemption, (2) human subjects involvement and characteristics, and (3) sources of materials. See Guidelines for the Review of Human Subjects for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children
rubrics_metrics.description: When the proposed project involves human subjects and/or NIH-defined clinical research, the committee will evaluate proposed plans for inclusion (or exclusion) of individuals on the basis of sex/gender, race, ethnicity, and children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine if inclusion/exclusion is justified in terms of the scientific goals and research strategy proposed. See Guidelines for the Review of Inclusion in Clinical Research for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee will evaluate involvement of live vertebrate animals according to five points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five points: (1) proposed use of the animals, and species, strains, ages, sex, and numbers to be used; (2) justifications for use of animals and appropriateness of species and numbers; (3) adequacy of veterinary care; (4) procedures for limiting discomfort, distress, pain and injury to that which is unavoidable (including use of analgesic, anesthetic, tranquilizing drugs and/or comfortable restraining devices); and (5) methods of euthanasia and reason for selection if not consistent with the AVMA Guidelines on Euthanasia. See Worksheet for Review of the Vertebrate Animal Section for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether materials or procedures proposed are potentially hazardous to research personnel and/or the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If hazards exist, determine whether adequate protection is proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: For Resubmissions, the committee will evaluate the application as now presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the responses to comments from the previous scientific review group and changes made to the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: For Renewals, the committee will consider the progress made in the last funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess accomplishments and whether renewal is justified by progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision
rubrics_metrics.description: For Revisions, the committee will consider the appropriateness of the proposed expansion of the scope of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Revision relates to a specific line of investigation presented in the original application that was not recommended for approval, consider whether responses to previous reviewer comments are adequate and whether substantial changes are clearly evident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications from Foreign Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether the project presents special opportunities through use of unusual talent, resources, populations, or environmental conditions that exist in other countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether these opportunities are not readily available in the United States or augment existing U.S. resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess the information provided in the Select Agent section of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate: (1) the Select Agent(s) to be used, (2) the registration status of all entities where Select Agent(s) will be used, (3) the procedures to monitor possession/use/transfer of Select Agent(s), and (4) plans for appropriate biosafety, biocontainment, and security of the Select Agent(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will comment on whether Resource Sharing Plans or rationale for not sharing are reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Types include: (1) Data Sharing Plan, (2) Sharing Model Organisms, and (3) Genome Wide Association Studies (GWAS) plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will consider whether the budget and the requested period of support are fully justified and reasonable in relation to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess adequacy and justification of requested funds and duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Comments to the Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may provide guidance to the applicant or recommend against resubmission without fundamental revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is discretionary feedback beyond scoring; may include specific suggestions or warnings about resubmission.
